title: Temperature as tick rate and surface quantity
html:
Classical statistical mechanics defines temperature implicitly through the Boltzmann distribution \rho \propto e^{-\beta H}, where \beta = 1/(k_B T) enforces energy conservation. In the QOU, \beta_q holds direct operational meaning: it counts the discrete Reeb operations composing one macroscopic time unit. Temperature is the tick rate of the quantum substrate, not a statistical average over kinetic energies.

Surface character of temperature. The entropy S_q(U) integrates strictly over the surface \partial U, guided by two principles.

First, the non-abelian Stokes theorem converts the bulk curvature integral to a boundary holonomy. The flatness conditions render this integral independent of the bounding surface choice. Entropy constitutes pure boundary datum.

Second, the Frobenius pairing is non-degenerate. Internal degrees of freedom are fully determined by boundary data via the categorical trace. The boundary \partial U controls the number of distinguishable states in U, encoding the content-object holographic principle. Temperature, as the energy derivative of entropy, strictly inherits this boundary character.

Classical limit. As q \to 1, T_q \to 0 and \beta_q \to \infty, sending S_q(U) \to S_{\mathrm{classical}}(U). The non-abelian Stokes integral degenerates to the classical Gauss law. The Frobenius trace becomes the ordinary matrix trace. The Boltzmann constant emerges as k_B = \hbar_q / T_{\mathrm{phys}} in the correspondence limit, where physical temperature T_{\mathrm{phys}} is measured in SI units.
